questions.question:
Read this email from your English-speaking friend Callum and the notes you have made.

From: Callum
Subject: Clean-up day

Hi!
Our town is having a clean-up day on Saturday the 14th, and I’ve put both our names down as helpers! [Note 1: Fantastic!] Volunteers can clean the park, the river bank or the streets near the station. Which one shall we choose? [Note 2: Tell Callum] The organisers say we should bring some things with us, but they didn’t say what. What do you think we need? [Note 3: Suggest] Afterwards there’s a free picnic for all the helpers. Do you want to stay for it? [Note 4: No, because …]

See you,
Callum

Write your email to Callum using all the notes. Write about 100 words.
questions.explanation:
A good answer replies to all four notes: (1) says you are pleased Callum put your names down; (2) chooses the park, the river bank or the streets near the station, and gives a reason; (3) suggests what to bring, for example gloves, bags or old clothes; (4) explains why you cannot stay for the picnic. Use an informal greeting and ending, link your ideas and write about 100 words.

Model answer:
Hi Callum,
That’s fantastic – thanks for putting my name down! It’s a really good way to help our town.
Let’s choose the river bank. I walk my dog there every morning and there’s always lots of plastic in the water. It makes me sad.
I think we should bring strong gloves, some big rubbish bags and old clothes, because it might be muddy. A bottle of water is a good idea too.
Unfortunately I can’t stay for the picnic. It’s my grandad’s birthday that afternoon and we’re having lunch at his house.
See you on the 14th,
Lucía

questions.question:
Choose ONE of these questions. Write your answer in about 100 words.

Question 2 – Article
You see this announcement in an English-language magazine for students.

Articles wanted!
HOW MY TOWN COULD BE GREENER
What is good about your town for the environment? What problems are there? What one change would make the biggest difference?
Write an article answering these questions. The best article will win a prize.

Write your article.

Question 3 – Story
Your English teacher has asked you to write a story.
Your story must begin with this sentence:
Nobody believed what we found in the river.

Write your story.
questions.explanation:
Article: give your article a title, answer all the questions in the announcement (what is good, what the problems are, one change you would make) and give reasons for your opinions. Story: begin with the given sentence, say what you found and how people reacted, and give the story a clear ending. Use past tenses consistently. In both tasks write about 100 words.

Model article:
A greener future for Westbridge
My town already does some things well. There are recycling bins on every street, and the old factory has become a lovely park.
However, there are still problems. The centre is full of cars, especially in the morning, and the air can be quite dirty. There also aren’t enough safe places to ride a bike.
If I could change one thing, I would close the main street to traffic and plant trees there. People could walk, cycle and meet their friends outside. Wouldn’t that be better for everyone?

Model story:
Nobody believed what we found in the river. It was during a school project, and my friend Sam and I were collecting rubbish near the old bridge.
Suddenly Sam pulled out a heavy metal box. Inside there were old coins and a letter dated 1923. We took everything to the town museum.
At first the staff thought it was a joke, but after a few days they called our school. The coins were real, and the letter had belonged to a local family.
Now our box is in the museum, with our names next to it!
